desc:
Collect all different non-empty substrings of s (a string that appears several times is listed once) and sort them in dictionary order, where a string comes before every longer string that starts with it (so "a" < "ab" < "b"). Return the k-th string of this list, counting from 1.

s = "banana"
sorted distinct substrings: a, an, ana, anan, anana, b, ba, ban, bana, banan, banana, n, na, nan, nana
k = 5  ->  "anana"
k = 8  ->  "ban"
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
1 ≤ k ≤ (number of different substrings of s), which is at most 4,501,500
hints: Generating and sorting all distinct substrings is correct, but there can be millions of them, each up to n characters long.
In the sorted order of the suffixes, the new distinct substrings contributed by each suffix (those not already prefixes of the previous suffix) appear in dictionary order, one block per suffix.

Suffix sa[t] contributes (n - sa[t]) - lcp[t-1] new substrings: its prefixes longer than the LCP with the previous suffix. Walk through the suffixes subtracting these block sizes from k until k falls into a block, then read the answer off that suffix.
editorial: Sort the suffixes. Every distinct substring is a prefix of its lexicographically smallest suffix-occurrence, namely of the first suffix in sorted order that starts with it. A prefix of suffix sa[t] of length L is new (not seen as a prefix of earlier suffixes) exactly when L > lcp[t-1], where lcp[t-1] is the common prefix length with the previous suffix. The new prefixes of suffix t are the strings of lengths lcp[t-1]+1 .. n-sa[t], and in dictionary order they all come after everything contributed by earlier suffixes and before everything contributed by later ones.

So scan t = 0, 1, ... with cnt = (n - sa[t]) - lcp[t-1] (taking lcp[-1] = 0): if k ≤ cnt the answer is s[sa[t] : sa[t] + lcp[t-1] + k], otherwise subtract cnt from k and continue. The suffix array costs O(n log2 n) and the scan O(n), plus O(n) to slice the answer. The total number of distinct substrings is the sum of all cnt values, which is the standard formula for counting distinct substrings.
